---
title: "Scoreboards & schedules"
description: "Pull a day of finished games with scores, then a full-season schedule — all executed live."
jupyter: python3
---

Two of the most common tasks are *"what games were played on date X?"* and
*"give me the whole season schedule."* Both are one function call, and both
return a tidy DataFrame. Every table on this page is executed against the live
ESPN API when the docs are built.

## A day of finished games

`espn_<sport>_scoreboard(dates=YYYYMMDD)` returns one row per game for that
date. We use a past date so the scores are final and stable:

```{python}
import polars as pl
pl.Config.set_tbl_rows(8)
pl.Config.set_tbl_cols(10)

from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_scoreboard

games = espn_nba_scoreboard(dates=20240110)
games.select(
    [
        "short_name",
        "home_display_name",
        "away_display_name",
        "home_score",
        "away_score",
        "status_type_detail",
        "home_winner",
    ]
).head(8)
```

The frame carries 50 columns in total — venue, broadcast, odds, and series
context all ride along — but the slice above is the human-readable core.

```{python}
n = games.shape[0]
home_wins = games.filter(pl.col("home_winner") == True).shape[0]
print(f"{n} games on 2024-01-10; the home team won {home_wins} of them.")
```

That count is computed at build time from the live frame — change the date and
the prose updates itself on the next render.

## A full-season schedule

Pass a season year instead of a date to get the whole schedule. The frame is
wide (every team, venue, and status field), so we select a readable slice:

```{python}
from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_schedule

schedule = espn_nba_schedule(dates=2024)
print(f"espn_nba_schedule(dates=2024) -> {schedule.shape[0]} games x {schedule.shape[1]} columns")

schedule.select(
    ["game_id", "season", "home_display_name", "away_display_name"]
).head(6)
```

## pandas, if you prefer

Any of these functions takes `return_as_pandas=True` and hands back a pandas
`DataFrame` with identical columns:

```{python}
teams_pd = espn_nba_scoreboard(dates=20240110, return_as_pandas=True)
print(type(teams_pd).__module__ + "." + type(teams_pd).__name__)
print(list(teams_pd.columns[:6]))
```
